indicator_definition: The farmland bird index measures changes in the population of bird species associated with farmland habitats, using 1990 as the base year (index = 100). A decline in farmland bird populations indicates biodiversity loss driven by agricultural intensification. Data are collected from national bird monitoring schemes.
rationale: The diversity of bird populations in agricultural landscapes is an indicator of the ecological health of farming systems. Stable or increasing bird populations signal that agricultural practices support biodiversity. Halting and reversing the decline in farmland bird populations is essential for sustainable food systems.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled from national breeding bird surveys and reported to Eurostat. The index aggregates population trends across a representative set of bird species typical of farmland habitats. Results are smoothed to account for year-to-year variability in survey counts.
